title: MINI-CHALLENGE: Complete Ship Validation Suite

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Time to prove your validation mastery. Create a comprehensive diagnostic that checks EVERYTHING—status, errors, thresholds, collections. Leave no system unverified."
story.requirements: Build a complete validation suite using all assertion types: equality, contains, boolean, numeric, length, and collection checks. This mirrors real-world test scenarios.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Outstanding! That's a production-grade validation suite. Chapter 1 complete—you can communicate, store data, and validate it. The ship's basic diagnostics are online. Now we organize complex test suites."

description: Create a comprehensive validation suite that integrates ALL Section 1.3 assertion concepts.
requirements: Use all 6+ assertion types learned in Section 1.3
Validate scalars with Should Be Equal
Validate boolean conditions with Should Be True/False
Validate numeric ranges with Should Be Greater/Less Than
Validate collection sizes with Length Should Be
Validate collection contents with List/Dictionary assertions
Demonstrate assertion keyword flexibility (lowercase or uppercase variation)
All assertions must pass for challenge to succeed
constraints: At least 6 different assertion keyword types
Must validate at least one list and one dictionary
Must include at least one numeric comparison
Must include at least one boolean check
At least one assertion keyword must use non-standard case (lowercase/uppercase)
All variables must follow naming conventions
instructions: Create *** Variables *** section with constants: ${SHIP_NAME} = 'Starlight Explorer', ${MAX_TEMP} = 100, ${MIN_POWER} = 50
Create *** Test Cases *** section with test named 'Complete Ship Validation'
Validate ship name: Create ${ship_name} and verify it equals ${SHIP_NAME}
Validate error message: Create ${error} = 'Critical hull breach in sector 7' and verify it contains 'breach'
Validate status report: Create ${report} = 'Diagnostic: 3 warnings, 1 critical error' and verify it contains 'critical'
Validate temperature: Create ${temp} = 75 and verify it's less than ${MAX_TEMP}
Validate power: Create ${power} = 60 and verify it's greater than ${MIN_POWER}
Validate boolean: Create ${repairs_done} = ${True} and verify it's True
Validate list: Create @{systems} with 5 items, verify length is 5, verify it contains 'Navigation'
Validate dictionary: Create &{status} with 3 pairs, verify it has key 'Power', verify it has key 'Navigation'
Demonstrate flexibility: Use at least one assertion in lowercase (e.g., 'should be equal') or uppercase
hints: *** Variables *** section must come before *** Test Cases ***
Use constants from *** Variables *** in your test
Don't forget to use ${list} notation with Length Should Be, not @{list}
All assertions must pass for the challenge to succeed
solution:
*** Variables ***
${SHIP_NAME}     Starlight Explorer
${MAX_TEMP}      100
${MIN_POWER}     50

*** Test Cases ***
Complete Ship Validation
    # Equality checks
    ${ship_name}           Set Variable    Starlight Explorer
    Should Be Equal        ${ship_name}    ${SHIP_NAME}
    
    # Substring checks
    ${error}               Set Variable    Critical hull breach in sector 7
    Should Contain         ${error}    breach
    
    ${report}              Set Variable    Diagnostic: 3 warnings, 1 critical error
    SHOULD CONTAIN         ${report}    critical
    
    # Numeric comparisons
    ${temp}                Set Variable    75
    Should Be Less Than    ${temp}    ${MAX_TEMP}
    
    ${power}               Set Variable    60
    Should Be Greater Than    ${power}    ${MIN_POWER}
    
    # Boolean check
    ${repairs_done}        Set Variable    ${True}
    Should Be True         ${repairs_done}
    
    # List validation
    @{systems}             Create List    Navigation    Power    Life Support    Communications    Sensors
    Length Should Be       ${systems}    5
    List Should Contain Value    ${systems}    Navigation
    
    # Dictionary validation
    &{status}              Create Dictionary    Navigation=OFFLINE    Power=CRITICAL    Life_Support=OPERATIONAL
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${status}    Power
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${status}    Navigation
    
    Log                    Complete validation suite passed!

theory.title: Section 1.3 Mini-Challenge: Comprehensive Validation Mastery
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 steps back, arms crossed, watching PROTO-7 approach the central diagnostic console.

"PROTO-7, this is your final test for Chapter 1. You've learned to communicate (Log), store data (Variables), and validate everything (Assertions). Now integrate all these skills into one comprehensive diagnostic suite."

PROTO-7's optics glow brighter. "A complete system validation. I'm ready."

What is a Comprehensive Validation Suite?

A validation suite is a test that checks multiple aspects of a system using different assertion types. In production testing, you rarely use just one type of assertion—you combine them to ensure complete coverage.

This challenge integrates:

  • ✅ Equality checks (Should Be Equal)
  • ✅ Substring validation (Should Contain)
  • ✅ Boolean logic (Should Be True/False)
  • ✅ Numeric comparisons (Should Be Greater/Less Than)
  • ✅ Length validation (Length Should Be)
  • ✅ Collection membership (List Should Contain Value)
  • ✅ Dictionary keys (Dictionary Should Contain Key)
  • ✅ Keyword flexibility (case-insensitive variations)

Why This Matters

Real-world test automation requires validating:

  • Configuration values match expectations (equality)
  • Error messages contain expected text (substring)
  • System states are correct (boolean)
  • Performance metrics are within range (numeric)
  • Data structures have correct size (length)
  • Collections contain expected items (membership)

This challenge simulates a real diagnostic test for a spaceship—the same principles apply to web apps, APIs, databases, or embedded systems.

Challenge Structure

1. Constants with *** Variables ***

Define reusable values at the top of your test file:

*** Variables ***
${SHIP_NAME}     Starlight Explorer
${MAX_TEMP}      100
${MIN_POWER}     50

Benefits of *** Variables *** section:

  • Centralized configuration
  • Easy to update thresholds
  • Reusable across multiple test cases
  • Clear documentation of important values

2. Comprehensive Test Case

One test case that validates multiple aspects:

*** Test Cases ***
Complete Ship Validation
    # Equality: Ship identity
    ${ship_name}    Set Variable    Starlight Explorer
    Should Be Equal    ${ship_name}    ${SHIP_NAME}

    # Substring: Error messages
    ${error}        Set Variable    Critical hull breach detected
    Should Contain    ${error}    breach

    # Boolean: Repair status
    ${repairs_done}    Set Variable    ${True}
    Should Be True    ${repairs_done}

    # Numeric: Temperature within range
    ${temp}         Set Variable    75
    Should Be Less Than    ${temp}    ${MAX_TEMP}

    # Numeric: Power above minimum
    ${power}        Set Variable    60
    Should Be Greater Than    ${power}    ${MIN_POWER}

    # Length: System count
    @{systems}      Create List    Nav    Power    Life Support    Comms    Sensors
    Length Should Be    ${systems}    5

    # List membership
    List Should Contain Value    ${systems}    Nav

    # Dictionary: System status
    &{status}       Create Dictionary    Navigation=OFFLINE    Power=CRITICAL
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${status}    Navigation
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${status}    Power

    Log    ✅ Complete validation suite passed!

Validation Coverage Matrix

Validation TypeKeywordWhat It Checks
Equality Should Be Equal Exact match (ship name)
Substring Should Contain Text contains keyword (error messages)
Boolean Should Be True Condition is True (repairs complete)
Threshold (Upper) Should Be Less Than Value below maximum (temperature)
Threshold (Lower) Should Be Greater Than Value above minimum (power)
Size Length Should Be Collection has exact count (5 systems)
Membership List Should Contain Value Item exists in list (Navigation)
Keys Dictionary Should Contain Key Key exists in dictionary (Power)

Demonstrating Keyword Flexibility

Remember: assertions are case-insensitive. Show your understanding by using at least one variation:

*** Test Cases ***
Flexibility Example
    ${status}    Set Variable    operational

    # Standard case
    Should Be Equal    ${status}    operational

    # Lowercase (demonstrates flexibility)
    should be equal    ${status}    operational

    # Uppercase (also valid)
    SHOULD CONTAIN     ${status}    oper

    # All ✅ valid!

Real-World Validation Patterns

Pattern 1: Configuration Validation

*** Variables ***
${API_TIMEOUT}     30
${MAX_RETRIES}     3

*** Test Cases ***
API Configuration Check
    &{config}       Create Dictionary    timeout=30    retries=3

    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${config}    timeout
    ${timeout}      Get From Dictionary    ${config}    timeout
    Should Be Equal    ${timeout}    ${API_TIMEOUT}

    Should Be Greater Than    ${timeout}    0
    Should Be Less Than       ${timeout}    60

Pattern 2: Error Handling Validation

*** Test Cases ***
Error Response Validation
    ${error_msg}    Set Variable    ERROR 404: Resource not found in database

    # Error code present
    Should Contain    ${error_msg}    ERROR 404

    # Error type identified
    Should Contain    ${error_msg}    not found

    # Message not empty
    Should Not Be Empty    ${error_msg}

    # Message length reasonable
    ${length}       Get Length    ${error_msg}
    Should Be Greater Than    ${length}    10

Pattern 3: System Health Check

*** Test Cases ***
System Health Validation
    # Performance metrics
    ${response_time}    Set Variable    250
    ${cpu_usage}        Set Variable    45
    ${memory_usage}     Set Variable    60

    # All within acceptable range
    Should Be Less Than    ${response_time}    500
    Should Be Less Than    ${cpu_usage}        80
    Should Be Less Than    ${memory_usage}     90

    # System operational
    ${system_up}        Set Variable    ${True}
    Should Be True      ${system_up}

    # Critical services running
    @{services}         Create List    API    Database    Cache
    Length Should Be    ${services}    3
    List Should Contain Value    ${services}    Database

Best Practices for Validation Suites

1. Group Related Validations

Organize assertions by what they validate:

*** Test Cases ***
Organized Validation
    # Configuration checks
    ${config_name}     Set Variable    Production
    Should Be Equal    ${config_name}    Production

    # Performance checks
    ${load_time}       Set Variable    2.5
    Should Be Less Than    ${load_time}    5.0

    # Data integrity checks
    @{records}         Create List    Rec1    Rec2    Rec3
    Length Should Be   ${records}    3

2. Use Descriptive Variable Names

*** Test Cases ***
Descriptive Names
    # ✅ Good: Clear intent
    ${current_temperature}    Set Variable    75
    ${maximum_safe_temp}      Set Variable    100
    Should Be Less Than       ${current_temperature}    ${maximum_safe_temp}

    # ❌ Less clear
    ${temp}    Set Variable    75
    ${max}     Set Variable    100
    Should Be Less Than    ${temp}    ${max}

3. Add Context with Logging

*** Test Cases ***
Contextual Logging
    ${reactor_temp}    Set Variable    85
    ${max_temp}        Set Variable    100

    Should Be Less Than    ${reactor_temp}    ${max_temp}
    Log    Reactor temperature ${reactor_temp}°C is safe (max: ${max_temp}°C)

    @{systems}         Create List    Nav    Power    Comms
    Length Should Be   ${systems}    3
    Log    All ${systems.__len__()} critical systems detected

4. Validate Dependencies First

Check prerequisites before detailed validation:

*** Test Cases ***
Dependency Order
    @{systems}         Create List    Nav    Power

    # First: Ensure list is not empty
    Should Not Be Empty    ${systems}

    # Then: Validate specific items
    List Should Contain Value    ${systems}    Nav

    # Finally: Check exact count
    Length Should Be    ${systems}    2

Challenge Grading Criteria

Your validation suite must:

  1. ✅ Define constants in *** Variables *** section
  2. ✅ Use at least 6 different assertion keyword types
  3. ✅ Perform at least 8 total assertions
  4. ✅ Validate at least one list
  5. ✅ Validate at least one dictionary
  6. ✅ Include at least one numeric comparison
  7. ✅ Include at least one boolean check
  8. ✅ Demonstrate keyword flexibility (use lowercase/uppercase variation)
  9. ✅ All assertions must pass
  10. ✅ Follow proper naming conventions

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Mistake 1: Using @{list} with Length Should Be

*** Test Cases ***
Length Validation
    @{systems}      Create List    Nav    Power

    # ❌ Wrong: Don't use @{} with Length Should Be
    Length Should Be    @{systems}    2

    # ✅ Correct: Use ${} notation
    Length Should Be    ${systems}    2

Mistake 2: Forgetting *** Variables *** Section

# ❌ Wrong: No *** Variables *** section
*** Test Cases ***
My Test
    ${SHIP_NAME}    Set Variable    Explorer    # Not a constant!

# ✅ Correct: Constants at top
*** Variables ***
${SHIP_NAME}    Starlight Explorer

*** Test Cases ***
My Test
    Should Be Equal    ${SHIP_NAME}    Starlight Explorer

Mistake 3: Case-Sensitive Value Comparison

*** Test Cases ***
Case Sensitivity
    ${status}    Set Variable    OPERATIONAL

    # ❌ Fails: Values are case-sensitive
    Should Be Equal    ${status}    operational

    # ✅ Passes: Exact match
    Should Be Equal    ${status}    OPERATIONAL

Success Indicators

You'll know you've succeeded when:

  • ✅ All assertions pass (no red errors in output)
  • ✅ Validation covers equality, substrings, booleans, numerics, lengths, and collections
  • ✅ Code is organized and readable
  • ✅ Constants are defined in *** Variables ***
  • ✅ At least one keyword uses non-standard case
  • ✅ Final log message confirms success

What You're Learning

This challenge teaches you to:

  1. Think holistically about test coverage
  2. Combine multiple assertion types for comprehensive validation
  3. Use constants effectively with *** Variables ***
  4. Organize validations logically within a test
  5. Apply keyword flexibility appropriately
  6. Write production-quality test code

After This Challenge

You'll have completed Chapter 1: First Contact! You now understand:

  • ✅ Section 1.1: Sequential execution and logging
  • ✅ Section 1.2: Variables (scalars, lists, dictionaries)
  • ✅ Section 1.3: Assertions (all major types)

Next up: Chapter 2 teaches you to organize complex test suites, create reusable keywords, and structure larger projects.

MENTOR-9: "This is it, PROTO-7. Build a complete validation suite with constants, equality checks, substring validation, boolean logic, numeric comparisons, length checks, list membership, and dictionary keys. Use all your knowledge. Show me you're ready for advanced testing. Make it pass."
